name: Sodium PCA
lead: Sodium PCA is the sodium salt of pyroglutamic acid (2-pyrrolidone-5-carboxylic acid, also called sodium pyroglutamate or sodium pidolate). It is used in cosmetics as a humectant, an ingredient that attracts and holds water, in dry-skin and hair products.[1]

Pyroglutamic acid is a natural component of the skin's natural moisturizing factor (NMF).[1] The Cosmetic Ingredient Review Expert Panel reassessed PCA and its salts, which it describes as functioning in cosmetics as skin-conditioning humectants.[2]
Very little clinical research on sodium PCA itself was found; it appears mostly as one ingredient within formulations.
infobox: Component of skin natural moisturizing factor[1]

paras: Pyroglutamic acid (C5H7NO3) forms when the free amino group of glutamic acid or glutamine cyclises into a lactam. In cells it arises from glutathione metabolism and is converted back to glutamate by 5-oxoprolinase.[1] It exists as D and L enantiomers.[1]
Wikipedia describes the sodium salt as having low toxicity and not being a skin irritant, with use limited by relatively high cost.[1]

Sodium PCA is used in moisturizers and hair products for its moisture-retaining properties.[1] Its presence in the skin's natural moisturizing factor is the usual rationale given for including it in dry-skin formulations.[1]

No clinical trial found tests sodium PCA alone for appearance outcomes. A pilot study of 25 adults with mild-to-moderate eczema tested an over-the-counter botanical eczema therapy, a formulation rather than sodium PCA specifically.[3] The Cosmetic Ingredient Review panel's 2019 safety assessment reviewed existing data on PCA and its sodium, calcium, magnesium and potassium salts.[2]
Laboratory research includes an in vitro study of lipid ordering in animal skin treated with sodium pyrrolidone carboxylate alongside penetration enhancers.[4]

card.summary: A skin-derived humectant salt used in moisturizers; safety is reviewed, but no appearance trials of the ingredient alone were found.

quick.overview:
Sodium PCA is a humectant found in many moisturizers, toners and hair products. It is the sodium salt of a compound the skin makes naturally as part of its moisture-retaining system.

It is rarely studied on its own, so evidence is mostly its safety review and its role in skin biology.
quick.mechanism: As a humectant it binds water. Pyroglutamic acid is a component of the skin's natural moisturizing factor, which is the basis for its use in dry-skin products.
quick.risks: Wikipedia describes it as low in toxicity and not a skin irritant. The Cosmetic Ingredient Review panel has reassessed PCA and its salts for cosmetic use.
